table_title: List 56 sovereign-state national capitals that sit on a single primary perennial river. Universe = every national capital city of a UN-member + observer-state that has its own standalone English Wikipedia article (from Wikipedia's 'List of national capitals' master article, bold sovereign-state rows; capitals without a standalone English article are out of scope under the source rule) filtered by the admission rule that each capital's own per-capital Wikipedia article foregrounds a single primary perennial river in the lede or infobox. The sovereign-state sweep is complete: 203 per-capital admission verdicts recorded across cycles 0–8 (56 PASS, 145 EXCLUDE with per-capital reasons documented in curation.json::source_coverage_notes::admission_gate_exclusions, plus 2 cycle-2 strict-gate-violation drops). Edge cases handled per audit-cycle amendments: confluence capitals excluded (14 — Belgrade Sava+Danube, Khartoum White+Blue Nile, Ottawa Ottawa+Rideau, Vilnius Vilnia+Neris, Phnom Penh Tonlé Sap+Mekong+Bassac, etc.); estuary capitals excluded (5 — Buenos Aires + Montevideo on Río de la Plata; Banjul on Gambia River estuary-island; Bissau on Geba River estuary; Georgetown on Demerara River estuary — applied consistently per cycle-5 audit BLOCKING); wadi-Riyadh excluded (1 — Wadi Hanifa is a seasonal wadi rather than perennial river per cycle-3 audit BLOCKING). Honduras: only Tegucigalpa staged — the live master list shows Tegucigalpa as the primary row entry with a co-official-capital note, AND a separate continuation row for Comayagüela sharing the Honduras/co-official context; Comayagüela has no standalone English Wikipedia article (the EN URL redirects to Tegucigalpa), so its continuation row is out of scope under the source rule per cycle-7 audit BLOCKING resolution in cycle-8.
db_analog: SELECT c.capital_name AS capital, co.country_name AS country, r.river_name AS river, co.continent FROM capitals c JOIN countries co ON c.country_id = co.country_id JOIN cities_on_rivers cor ON c.capital_id = cor.capital_id JOIN rivers r ON cor.river_id = r.river_id WHERE c.capital_id IN (curator_rebuilt_sovereign_state_capital_ids_with_single_foregrounded_river) ORDER BY co.continent ASC, c.capital_name ASC
temporal_note: Wikipedia 'List of national capitals' master article (universe-anchor for sovereign-state capital + country + continent, 3 of 4 cells) + 56 per-capital Wikipedia articles (admission-gate + River cell, 1 of 4 cells), all accessed 2026-05-15 / 2026-05-16. Universe = 56 curator-rebuilt sovereign-state capitals (claim_type = `candidate_rebuild`) — the master 'List of national capitals' supplies the deterministic UN-member + observer-state capital universe, but the master does NOT carry a River column. The 'sits on a single primary perennial river' subset is rebuilt entirely from per-capital prose per the strict admission rule. The instance is keyed by Capital (not by sovereign-state master row); for sovereign-state rows naming multiple co-official capital cities, every co-official capital that has its own standalone English Wikipedia article AND independently passes the strict gate is staged as a separate row. The sovereign-state sweep is COMPLETE: every sovereign-state capital + every co-official joint-capital with a standalone article + Taiwan/Kosovo (contested-sovereign) has a per-capital admission verdict. Exact accounting: 56 staged INCLUDE + 145 per-capital-verified EXCLUDE + 2 cycle-2 strict-gate-violation drops = 203 per-capital admission verdicts. temporal_sensitivity = low because (a) river geography is stable on benchmark timescales; (b) capital-of-each-country occasionally changes (Astana ↔ Nur-Sultan recent rename; Naypyidaw new capital) but staged set anchored at 2026-05-15. Per-row Capital + Country + Continent are sourced from the master list per audit-cycle-1 amendment #4 (source-role separation: master defines 3 of 4 cells deterministically; per-capital article defines the 4th cell + admission). Per-row River is sourced from the per-capital Wikipedia article's lede or infobox where it foregrounds a single primary perennial river; River values use the article-foregrounded form (typically the bare river name without the 'River' suffix, e.g., 'Thames', 'Seine', 'Danube', 'Nile'; with the suffix retained only where needed to disambiguate from the city itself or country — 'Kabul River', 'Suriname River', 'Roseau River' to avoid PK or country ambiguity). Joint-capital handling per normalization_decisions: Pretoria from the slash-row 'Bloemfontein/Cape Town/Pretoria' South Africa entry; La Paz from the slash-row 'La Paz/Sucre' Bolivia entry; Tegucigalpa from the Honduras row (master shows Tegucigalpa as the primary row entry with a co-official-capital note AND a separate continuation row for Comayagüela sharing the Honduras/co-official context, NOT a slash-row). Cycle-3 audit BLOCKING #2 dropped Riyadh (Wadi Hanifa is a seasonal wadi rather than perennial river). Cycle-5 audit BLOCKING #1 dropped Bissau (Geba River estuary) + Georgetown (Demerara River estuary) for consistency with Buenos Aires + Montevideo + Banjul estuary-EXCLUDE precedent. Cycle-7 audit BLOCKING (scope) added Comayagüela (Honduras, Choluteca) — the instance is keyed by Capital and Comayagüela independently passes the strict gate per its own per-capital article ('Tegucigalpa and Comayagüela, being sister cities, are physically separated by the Choluteca River'). Cycle-8 audit BLOCKING (factual) reversed: the EN URL for Comayagüela redirects to Tegucigalpa (no standalone English article exists), so Comayagüela fails the source rule's standalone-article requirement and is OUT of scope. Comayagüela was dropped from staged set in cycle-8; only Tegucigalpa is staged for Honduras. Admission-gate exclusions are exhaustively enumerated in curation.json::source_coverage_notes::admission_gate_exclusions.
_extraction_notes: Implicit_join instance — capital-to-river relationship is not declared in any master capital-list table; the join target (river) is resolved per-capital from each capital's own Wikipedia article. Brings `implicit_join` from 5/8 (gap-3) to 6/8 (gap-2); needs 2 more after this to saturate at 8/8. Geography/Cities EXISTING subdomain — Geography family extends from 12 to 13 instances with this Ready. NEW `cities-and-capitals/national-capitals` fine-class — bucket extends from 1 to 2 instances. Source universe = 56 sovereign-state capitals selected from the FULL set of UN-member + observer-state capitals (Wikipedia 'List of national capitals' master, bold sovereign-state rows). Each row is a Capital with its own standalone English Wikipedia article (the source-rule requirement); for sovereign-state master rows that enumerate multiple co-official capital cities, each capital with a standalone article is independently evaluated. Schema: 4 cols (Capital PK + Country categorical + River categorical + Continent categorical closed 6-value). Sort: Continent ASC primary (Africa→Asia→Europe→North America→South America; Oceania empty), Capital ASC alphabetical secondary. Continent distribution: Africa 9, Asia 13, Europe 23, North America 6, South America 5, Oceania 0 = 56. Europe accounts for 23 of 56 (41%); the cycle-3 sweep added 9 non-European INCLUDEs net (Juba/Pretoria/Rabat in Africa; Thimphu in Asia; Tegucigalpa in NA; Caracas/La Paz/Paramaribo in SA; plus Manila cycle-2 in Asia) vs. 1 European (Vaduz); cycle-4 sweep added 5 more non-European INCLUDEs net (Havana/Kingston/Roseau/Santo Domingo in NA Caribbean; Ulaanbaatar in Asia), dropping Riyadh per audit-cycle-3 BLOCKING #2 (wadi-not-river framing); cycle-5 dropped Bissau (Africa) + Georgetown (SA) per audit-cycle-4 BLOCKING #1 (estuary-policy consistency); cycle-7 added Comayagüela (Honduras, NA) per audit-cycle-6 BLOCKING (Capital-keyed framing) but cycle-8 reverted that add per audit-cycle-7 BLOCKING (factual): Comayagüela's EN Wikipedia URL redirects to the Tegucigalpa article — no standalone EN article exists, so Comayagüela fails the source rule and is now OUT of scope. Sovereign-state sweep is COMPLETE: every UN-member sovereign-state capital with a standalone EN article + every co-official joint-capital with a standalone EN article + Taiwan/Kosovo contested-sovereign cases all have a per-capital admission verdict. Exact final accounting: 56 staged INCLUDE + 145 per-capital-verified EXCLUDE + 2 cycle-2 strict-gate-violation drops = 203 per-capital admission verdicts. Pre-curation design pass committed 8 amendments BEFORE staging — most load-bearing: (1) claim_type = candidate_rebuild (NOT partially_supplemented — the inclusion predicate is rebuilt from per-capital prose; master cannot define the target subset); (2) strict single-river admission gate is a rebuilt selection rule (NOT source-derived filter); (3) Buenos Aires excluded under 'river' framing (Río de la Plata is estuary per its own article); (4) source-role separation: master for Capital+Country+Continent (3 of 4 cells), per-capital for River+admission (1 of 4 cells); (5) sovereign-state filter applied (bold UN-member + observer-state rows only); (6) 4-column schema kept; (7) per-river articles used only for audit cross-checking, NOT row-defining sources. Bridges + dams + ports + airports + battles + empires + philosophical-schools cycle lessons applied upfront: (a) single PK on Capital using Wikipedia common-form names per per-capital article title (diacritics preserved — Chișinău, Asunción, Dâmbovița, Bîc, Washington D.C. with periods); (b) per-row data sourced from 2 articles each (master + per-capital), 57 URLs total; (c) strict admission gating — cycle-1 audit found 2 staged rows (Bratislava, Minsk) violating the gate per article literal text; cycle-2 dropped both; cycle-3 added 10 new INCLUDEs (including Riyadh/Wadi Hanifa, later dropped); cycle-4 sweep added 7 INCLUDEs (Havana/Almendares, Kingston/Hope, Roseau/Roseau River, Santo Domingo/Ozama, Bissau/Geba River, Georgetown/Demerara, Ulaanbaatar/Tuul) and dropped Riyadh per audit-cycle-3 BLOCKING #2 (wadi-not-perennial-river framing); cycle-5 dropped Bissau + Georgetown per audit-cycle-4 BLOCKING #1 (estuary-policy consistency); cycle-7 added Comayagüela per audit-cycle-6 BLOCKING (Capital-keyed instance + co-official joint-capital framing); cycle-8 dropped Comayagüela per audit-cycle-7 BLOCKING (factual: EN URL redirects to Tegucigalpa, no standalone article — fails source rule); (d) candidate_rebuild claim type — 5th instance of this claim_type in pkdb_bench (joins philosophical-schools, religious-traditions, western-philosophers, architectural-styles); (e) source-role separation per amendment #4: master defines Capital + Country + Continent deterministically; per-capital article defines River + admission decision only; (f) consistent estuary-EXCLUDE rule with row-defining framing test: the article's PRIMARY current-location sentence in the lede (or the infobox's primary geographic descriptor) is checked for the word 'estuary'. Capitals whose primary current-location sentence uses 'estuary' are EXCLUDED (Buenos Aires + Montevideo on Río de la Plata; Banjul on Gambia River estuary-island; Bissau on Geba River estuary; Georgetown on Demerara River estuary). Capitals whose primary current-location sentence uses 'mouth' or 'on the [River]' are INCLUDED — Amsterdam ('founded at the mouth of the Amstel River'), Riga ('at the mouth of the Daugava river'), Rabat ('at the mouth of the river Bou Regreg'), Lisbon ('on the northern shore of the River Tagus'). Some of these INCLUDED articles do mention 'estuary' elsewhere in body/history text (Amsterdam's founding history references a 'wide estuary'; Lisbon's history section mentions 'Tagus River estuary'), but those non-row-defining mentions don't trigger the rule — only the article's primary current-location framing does. Joint-capital handling (Capital-keyed framing per audit-cycle-6 ruling + standalone-article source-rule per audit-cycle-7 ruling): each capital with its own standalone English Wikipedia article is independently evaluated against the strict gate; capitals that pass are staged as separate rows. South Africa master row enumerates Bloemfontein/Cape Town/Pretoria as joint capitals, each with its own standalone article: Pretoria PASS (Apies); Bloemfontein + Cape Town fail. Bolivia master row enumerates La Paz/Sucre, each with its own standalone article: La Paz PASS (Choqueyapu); Sucre fails. Honduras: live master list shows Tegucigalpa as the primary row entry with a co-official-capital note AND a separate continuation row for Comayagüela sharing the Honduras/co-official context; only Tegucigalpa has a standalone English Wikipedia article (Comayagüela's EN URL redirects to the Tegucigalpa article), so only Tegucigalpa is in scope and is staged on the Choluteca. Other joint-capital cases (Benin Cotonou/Porto-Novo; Malaysia Kuala Lumpur/Putrajaya; Sri Lanka Colombo/SJK; Burundi Gitega/Bujumbura) all have standalone articles for both/all co-officials, but their per-capital articles all fail the strict gate. Documented in curation.json::normalization_decisions. Entity class: `cities-and-capitals/national-capitals` (NEW fine-class extending the under-represented `cities-and-capitals` bucket from 1 to 2 instances).
